references.text: Jesus' direct call to the disciples to take up their cross and follow him, with the promise that whoever loses their life for his sake will find it, is a direct application of the principle of the grain.

Mark repeats Jesus' words that whoever wants to save their life will lose it, while whoever loses their life for the gospel will save it, as a clear parallel to the death and fruitfulness of the grain.
Paul uses the death of the grain as an image of the resurrection, where what is sown is not the body that will be, but a kernel that must die to receive new life, exactly as in John 12:24.
Immediately before the image of the grain is introduced, Jesus speaks of his hour having come for the Son of Man to be glorified, which happens through death and resurrection, just like the grain.

Jesus' explanation of the principle of the grain by saying that whoever loves their life will lose it, while whoever hates their life in this world will keep it for eternal life, elaborates on the mechanism in verse 24.
